expectation: GrzB is a cytoplasmic, granular stain in cytotoxic T and NK cells. It should mark a minority of small round cells, scattered singly or in clusters in stroma and tumour, with no signal in the nuclei of other cells and no diffuse tissue-wide haze.
observed: A: many sparse, discrete, cell-sized yellow dots on dark background, with density varying a lot between cores (dense in some, near-empty in others). B/C: only a few isolated bright cell-sized spots. D: compact bright blobs the size of single cells. A few cores show faint diffuse haze.
why: Discrete cell-sized positive cells in a minority of cells, with core-to-core variation in density, fit a rare cytotoxic population rather than haze or speckle.
